sources.entry: goploader - Easy file sharing with server-side encryption, curl/httpie/wget compliant. (Source Code) MIT Go

summary.one_liner: goploader is a file-sharing tool made of a Go server and a Go command-line client, aimed at sharing files easily from a terminal or a web browser.
summary.what_it_does: goploader is a file-sharing project with two parts, a server and a client, both written in Go. The client, built as the gpldr binary, is meant for sharing files from a terminal. The server can be run as a standalone binary (goploader-server) or as a Docker image. The README describes a setup web interface served by the server for use from a browser. The project states that it works with curl, httpie and wget, and the awesome-selfhosted entry describes server-side encryption. The README gives no detail on how uploads, links, or expiry work. Full documentation is referenced as hosted on the project's GitHub Pages site.
use_cases: share a file from the terminal
upload files with curl or wget
share files without using a terminal
run a file upload server in Docker
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into goploader
notable: Separate Go client (gpldr) and server (goploader-server) binaries
Stated compatibility with curl, httpie and wget
Docker image built with make docker
Setup web interface served by the server
caveats: The README warns that most of the technology used is now outdated and the project is maintained as is, so use is at the user's own risk
Building from source requires a local Go installation; Docker is needed for the container route
